identity.title: 15,16-Dihydrotanshinone I, a novel beta-catenin-targeting inhibitor that inhibits its nuclear translocation and reduces downstream CD36 expression in cancer.

content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Wnt/beta-catenin signaling drives many cancers; however, current inhibition strategies have limitations. Direct beta-catenin inhibitors that block nuclear translocation represent an alternative therapeutic approach. We used colorectal cancer (CRC) as a study model, over 90% of the CRC cases harbor mutations in this pathway. Here, we aim to explore the potential of 15,16-dihydrotanshinone-I (DHTS) as a beta-catenin inhibitor in cancer. METHODS: Molecular docking, biolayer interferometry assay and cellular thermal shift assay were used to examine the binding between DHTS and beta-catenin. Site-directed mutagenesis, in vitro and in vivo studies were used to examine the anti-CRC effects of DHTS following its binding to beta-catenin. RESULTS: We demonstrate, for the first time, that DHTS significantly reduces nuclear beta-catenin levels and transcriptional activity in CRC without affecting beta-catenin protein stability or conformation. DHTS binds to beta-catenin at Ser411. A point mutation at Ser411 disrupts this binding and abolishes the ability of DHTS to suppress nuclear beta-catenin, indicating that Ser411 binding is critical for blocking beta-catenin nuclear translocation. Furthermore, we identify CD36, a transmembrane fatty acid translocase, as a downstream beta-catenin target. DHTS reduces CD36 expression and cellular ATP levels in CRC cells; the reductions are reversed by beta-catenin overexpression or stabilization. In CRC-bearing mouse model, DHTS-loaded PLGA-PEG nanoparticles significantly reduce nuclear beta-catenin and CD36 expressions in tumors and inhibit tumor growth, consistent with the in vitro findings. CONCLUSIONS: Our study not only reveals the importance of Ser411 in beta-catenin function but also paves the path for developing DHTS as a beta-catenin inhibitor for CRC therapy.
